synergies: Because this card has Sly, cards that discard (such as Survivor or Prepared) allow it to be automatically played for free.
order: The doubled [Defend intent] Block from Shadowmeld applies after Dexterity.
notes: Thorns are especially useful against enemies that have attacks with multiple hits, such as Entomancer.
Dexterity only affects [Defend intent] Block gained directly from playing cards. Sources like Afterimage, Relics, and Potions are not affected.
Cards that do not list a base amount of [Defend intent] Block to gain ( Mirage, Entrench, etc.) are also unaffected.
Outbreak causes Poison to trigger and count down as part of its resolution. Having Accelerant causes it to trigger and count down additional times.

synergies: Phantom Blades allows Shivs to be retained until Accuracy is played, making their damage less reliant on drawing Accuracy before any Shiv cards.
**Acrobatics** is very useful in Sly decks, since it can dig for a Sly card and discard it immediately if one is drawn.
Outside of Sly decks, **Acrobatics** is still efficient card draw. It can also discard unwanted cards, including harmful Status and Curse cards like Burn and Doubt.
anti: Fiddle makes the player unable to draw during their turn, and **Acrobatics** will still discard a card even if it cannot draw.
notes: The discarded card can be from among the cards drawn by **Acrobatics** or a card that was already in Hand.
**Acrobatics** will always discard a card during its resolution, even if cards could not be drawn due to the hand limit, No Draw, or Fiddle.
If **Acrobatics** is played multiple times in a row due to an effect like Burst, each play draws and discards before the next play begins to resolve.
For instance, playing **Acrobatics** twice in a row with Burst causes the player to draw 3 cards, discard 1 card, draw 3 more cards, then discard 1 card again.

synergies: All for One returns all 0 cost **Adaptive Strikes** from the Discard Pile to the Hand, and Hologram can return a single copy or All for One itself.

Note that All for One returns 0 cost cards in the order that they were put into the Discard Pile. If other 0 cost cards were put there before creating **Adaptive Strikes**, those cards will return first, and the hand limit may prevent the player from returning all **Adaptive Strikes** to the Hand.
Feral allows a 0 copy to be played multiple times.
Anointed adds every **Adaptive Strike** from the Draw Pile to the Hand.
Anointed+ has Retain, allowing the player to save it until the Draw Pile shuffles.
Strike Dummy and Strike Dummy??? cause all **Adaptive Strikes** to deal 3 / 1 extra damage, respectively.
anti: In a thick deck (particularly a Status-focused deck), drawing the copied **Adaptive Strikes** will be difficult without excellent draw power.
Conversely, in an especially thin deck, **Adaptive Strike** can bloat the deck more easily.
If **Adaptive Strike** has Perfect Fit, ALL **Adaptive Strikes** will return to the top of the Draw Pile when shuffling.
notes: The original **Adaptrive Strike's** cost does not change.
All copies of **Adaptive Strike** maintain the original's Upgrade and Enchantment (if any), as well as in-battle modifications (other than changes to **Adaptive Strike's** cost).

**Adaptive Strike** copies itself before it resolves, so Enchantments that only work once per combat (such as Swift and Sown) will be applied to the copy before they are used up. The original will still use up the Enchantment, but the copy will be able to trigger it again.
**Adaptive Strike** copies itself before Razor Tooth can Upgrade it, so the copy will not be Upgraded if the original was not.

synergies: Afterimage is most powerful in Shiv and Sly decks, which tend to play many cards per turn that often do not gain [Defend intent] Block.
In decks with long combos, excess [Defend intent] Block can be preserved with Blur.
Bullet Time can play the entire Hand at once, usually triggering Afterimage at least 5 times.
order: Afterimage only gains [Defend intent] Block once the played card fully resolves. If the played card is an Attack, Afterimage will not trigger in time to block Thorns damage.
notes: [Defend intent] Block gained from Afterimage is not affected by Dexterity or Frail. It only scales with the number of Afterimage stacks.

If a card's effect plays another card(s) (such as using a card like Prepared to discard a Sly card), Afterimage only triggers after the original card resolves, and it gains [Defend intent] Block for each card played.
If a card is played multiple times in a row, such as by Burst or Replay, Afterimage gains [Defend intent] Block after each play.

synergies: Summon increases the HP/Max HP of Osty, which increases the damage of Unleash and Protector
Summon increases the damage potential of Necro Mastery
Summon will revive Osty, which enables all Osty-related cards
Summon increases the amount of [Defend intent] Block gained from Sacrifice
order: Playing Bone Shards after **Afterlife** will waste Osty's HP gain

synergies: Aggression can guarantee an Attack card is in Hand for Rage, One-Two Punch, and similar effects this turn.
Having an extra Attack in the Hand can make Juggling easier to trigger this turn.
Cards like Rampage and Thrash that gain value from repeated plays can be added by Aggression for another play.
Non-Attack cards and effects that Exhaust other cards, such as True Grit and Burning Pact, can eliminate weak Attack cards to reduce Aggression's variability.
Miniature Cannon causes Attacks Upgraded by Aggression to deal 3 additional damage.
Music Box will almost always have an Attack that it can create an Ethereal copy of.
An Attack Enchanted with Momentum from Punch Dagger can be added by Aggression to scale faster.
anti: Anger can quickly fill the Discard Pile with copies, making Aggression unlikely to return other more valuable Attacks.
Returning an Attack to the Hand each turn makes it harder to play Impatience and Restlessness.
order: Aggression returns the random Attack(s) to the Hand before drawing cards for the turn.
notes: As long as any Attacks are in the Discard Pile at the start of the turn, returning one with Aggression is mandatory.
Adding an Attack to the Hand does not count as drawing it. Hellraiser will not play that card even if it is a Strike card, and it will not count towards gaining from Automation.

synergies: Burst, Decisions, Decisions, Echo Form, Transfigure, Hidden Gem, and Duplicator can generate additional random Potions.
notes: **Alchemize** cannot create Fruit Juice.
**Alchemize** can create Entropic Brew, which can create Fruit Juice, but only when used outside of combat.
**Alchemize** cannot be generated during combat (via other Cards, Relics, or Potions).
If the player has no available potion slots when playing **Alchemize**, it resolves and Exhausts without effect.

synergies: Spending Stars to play Alignment triggers Black Hole, Child of the Stars, and Galactic Dust.
This will also trigger Mini Regent, provided it's the first instance of spending Stars for the turn.

**All for One** synergizes with most 0 cost cards: Beam Cell, Claw, Go for the Eyes, Boost Away, Hotfix, TURBO, FTL, Tesla Coil, Boot Sequence, Chill, Overclock, Helix Drill, Reboot, and Supercritical all cost 0 at base.
**All for One** synergizes with most 0 cost cards: Dualcast+, Zap+, Double Energy+, and Quadcast+ cost 0 once Upgraded.
**All for One** synergizes with most 0 cost cards: Momentum Strike, Adaptive Strike, and Rocket Punch can reduce their costs to 0 .
Hologram can retrieve **All for One** to play it again.
If a card is "free to play this combat", e.g. from Metamorphosis or Touch of Insanity, **All for One** will be able to return it from the Discard Pile.

By having TURBO and making Hologram+ free, **All for One** creates an infinite loop this combat. Hologram+ returns **All for One** to the Hand, which can then be played using the gained by TURBO to return both cards to the Hand.
notes: **All for One** returns 0 cost cards in the Discard Pile to the Hand in the order they were put there (oldest first). Any cards that would exceed the hand size limit of 10 cards will attempt to return to the Hand and are put back into the Discard Pile.
When viewing the Discard Pile, cards are displayed in the order they were put there. The 0 cost cards at the top of the list will be the first ones returned by **All for One**.

Having Free Power from Synthesis or having Brilliant Scarf active will only affect Power cards' costs in the Hand and in play. Their costs in the Discard Pile are not affected, and **All for One** will not return Power cards from the Discard Pile to the Hand while these effects are active (unless those Power cards already cost 0 , such as Subroutine+).

synergies: Since having a lot of **Angers** in the deck will reduce the chance to draw non-**Anger** cards, Headbutt can return key cards from the Discard Pile to the Draw Pile to guarantee they can be played again quickly.
Once the deck contains a large number of **Angers**, Unceasing Top is very likely to draw more **Angers** when it triggers, which can be played for free and draw even more cards.
anti: If **Anger** is Enchanted with Perfect Fit, ALL copies return to the top of the Draw Pile when shuffling.
order: **Anger** copies itself before Razor Tooth can Upgrade it, so the copy will not be Upgraded if the original was not.
All copies of **Anger** maintain the original's Upgrade and Enchantment (if any), as well as in-battle modifications.

**Anger** copies itself before it resolves, so Enchantments that only work once per combat (such as Swift and Sown) will be applied to the copy before they are used up. The original will still use up the Enchantment, but the copy will be able to trigger it again.

If **Anger** is Enchanted with Momentum from Punch Dagger, the effect "Increase this card's damage by 5" applies after **Anger** has already copied itself. The original's damage will increase, but the copy will not inherit that damage increase.

synergies: Each character has a 0 cost Rare card that gains . Having them with **Anointed** makes it easier to play expensive Rare cards like the signature "Form" Powers.
Multiple Rare cards have Retain (or gain it when Upgraded).
**Anointed+** can be Retained to fetch multiple free copies of Adaptive Strike once they shuffle back into the Draw Pile.
Royal Stamp can Royally Approve **Anointed** to make it Innate.
Electric Shrymp from Orobas can Imbue **Anointed** to automatically play it at the start of combat, effectively making all Rare cards Innate.
notes: Only cards in the Draw Pile are added to the Hand. The Discard Pile and Exhaust Pile are unaffected.
Rare cards are added to the Hand from the Draw Pile in the order they would be drawn (top to bottom).
If adding all Rare cards to the Hand would exceed the hand limit of 10 cards, the excess Rare cards remain in the Draw Pile.
**Anointed** itself leaves the Hand when played, so there will always be room for at least one Rare card.

synergies: Lantern and other sources of extra Energy on the first turn make it easier to play **Apotheosis** along with other cards.
Anchor provides [Defend intent] Block on the first turn, leaving more Energy available to play **Apotheosis**.
If the player can Forge on the first turn, **Apotheosis** will Upgrade Sovereign Blade, reducing its cost to 1 for the rest of combat.

Having **Apotheosis** removes the need to Upgrade cards at Rest Sites, except to Upgrade cards that become Innate and to Upgrade **Apotheosis** itself. This makes it much easier to use Girya and Shovel.
anti: Armaments and Drain Power become redundant with **Apotheosis** unless the player creates more cards mid-combat.

**Apotheosis** becomes progressively less relevant the more cards that are already Upgraded. If the player only has a few cards remaining that are worth Upgrading, **Apotheosis** will not be worthwhile.
Miniature Tent makes it possible to rest and Upgrade a card at Rest Sites, but **Apotheosis** almost completely removes the need to Upgrade anything.
notes: **Apotheosis** leaves the Hand when played but does not Exhaust until it resolves. It will never Upgrade itself.

Additionally, if it is played by another card (such as Havoc or Cascade), that card will still be in play when **Apotheosis** resolves. It will not be Upgraded, nor will any other cards currently in play.
**Apotheosis** only Upgrades cards that existed when it was played. Cards created afterwards, such as Shivs and Sweeping Gaze, will not be Upgraded.

synergies: **Armaments** can be used to Upgrade Power cards and cards with Exhaust before they are played.
Similarly, Upgrading cards with effects outside of combat is very useful, such as Feed, Not Yet, and Hand of Greed.
notes: **Armaments** leaves the Hand when played. It cannot Upgrade itself (though multiple copies of **Armaments** can Upgrade each other).
**Armaments** cannot apply to cards that are already Upgraded. When playing **Armaments**, the player must choose a non-Upgraded card to Upgrade.
Upgrading a card is not optional. If the player plays **Armaments**, they must Upgrade a card in Hand.

This can be relevant for cards that lose Exhaust when Upgraded, such as Thinking Ahead and Discovery. In some uncommon situations, it may be beneficial to allow these cards to Exhaust to thin the deck.

If **Armaments** Upgrades a card whose cost decreases when Upgraded, the card's current cost is set to that reduced cost. However, if that card's cost was randomized by Confused, Snecko Oil, or Slither, its cost will not become its reduced Upgraded cost if its current randomized cost is already lower.
For instance, if a non-Upgraded Stampede (which costs 2 and 1 when Upgraded) has its cost randomized: If its cost is currently 3 , **Armaments** reduces its cost to 1 when Upgrading it.
For instance, if a non-Upgraded Stampede (which costs 2 and 1 when Upgraded) has its cost randomized: If its cost is currently 0 , **Armaments** does not affect its cost.

For instance, if a non-Upgraded Stampede (which costs 2 and 1 when Upgraded) has its cost randomized: Note that if the card's cost is also being increased by another effect (such as Spiked Gauntlets or Tangled), those effects will apply after the Upgraded card's cost changes. In the example above, having Spiked Gauntlets would cause Stampede's cost to be 3 (2 when Upgraded), and the randomization would be between 1 and 4 .
Status and Curse cards cannot be Upgraded.
Aeonglass creates and Upgrades Wither cards, but they can only be Upgraded by Aeonglass itself.

synergies: Cards that transform cards in combat (such as BEGONE! or CHARGE!!) count as creating cards, and will trigger Arsenal.

Although it is generally harmful, Ascender's Bane can provide some niche benefits: Pact's End requires at least 3 cards in the Exhaust pile before it can be played, and Ascender's Bane means that one self-exhausting card is already available in the starting deck.
Although it is generally harmful, Ascender's Bane can provide some niche benefits: Ashen Strike deals 3 (4) extra damage after **Ascender's Bane** has been Exhausted.

Although it is generally harmful, Ascender's Bane can provide some niche benefits: **Ascender's Bane** Exhausting itself triggers Dark Embrace, Feel No Pain, Charon's Ashes, and Forgotten Soul, and it counts towards Joss Paper.
Although it is generally harmful, Ascender's Bane can provide some niche benefits: Pagestorm draws an additional card when Ascender's Bane is drawn.
anti: Discarding **Ascender's Bane** will prevent it from Exhausting at the end of the turn.
Attempting to Transform **Ascender's Bane** with Entropy will simply Transform it into a random other Curse card.
Havoc, Cascade, and Mayhem can have their effects wasted by **Ascender's Bane**.
order: Ethereal cards Exhaust themselves at the same time that the Hand is discarded at the end of the turn. If this triggers Dark Embrace, any cards drawn will not be discarded and can be played during the next turn.

synergies: Cards like Second Wind, Stoke, Fiend Fire, and Purity can Exhaust multiple cards at once.
Stoke is notable for creating cards equal to the amount it Exhausts. Since Stoke itself does not Exhaust, it can be played repeatedly to create a massive Exhaust Pile, even without a thick deck.
Numerous Status and Curse cards have Ethereal and will Exhaust from the Hand at the end of turn, scaling **Ashen Strike** passively. They can also serve as fodder for manually Exhausting cards.
Having Hellraiser causes **Ashen Strike** to play against a random enemy immediately when drawn.
Having Corruption causes ALL Skills to cost 0 and Exhaust when played, rapidly scaling **Ashen Strike's** damage.
Strike Dummy / Strike Dummy??? increase **Ashen Strike's** damage by 3 / 1, respectively.

Music Box creates an Ethereal copy of the first Attack card played this turn. Any unplayed Ethereal Attacks in Hand will Exhaust at the end of turn and contribute to **Ashen Strike's** damage, or **Ashen Strike** itself can be copied once enough cards are Exhausted.

Having Pael's Eye allows the player to Exhaust their whole Hand and start an extra turn once per combat. While normally meant as a mulligan, this can Exhaust many cards for free to increase **Ashen Strike's** damage.
The Instinct Enchantment from Tri-Boomerang doubles **Ashen Strike's** final listed damage. Each Exhausted card will increase its damage by 6 (8).
Ashwater and Glowwater Potion can Exhaust several cards at once
Soldier's Stew adds Replay 1 to all "Strike" cards this combat.
The Corrupted Enchantment from the Symbiote increases **Ashen Strike's** final listed damage by 50% and causes 2 HP loss when played.
Though the damage boost from Corrupted is weaker than Instinct, the extra HP loss gives **Ashen Strike** synergy with effects such as Rupture and Self-Forming Clay.
notes: If **Ashen Strike** is generated during combat (via other Cards, Relics or Potions), its damage will already be scaled based on the amount of cards in the Exhaust Pile.
If cards leave the Exhaust Pile, **Ashen Strike's** damage will reduce accordingly.

This is only possible when gaining another character's cards, such as via Prismatic Gem. The Ironclad cannot normally move cards from the Exhaust Pile to somewhere else, but cards like Summon Forth and Eidolon can.

synergies: Assassinate can ensure that other Innate Attacks (such as Backstab & Suppress) will benefit from additional Vulnerable damage (provided the enemy does not have Artifact).
Unsettling Lamp can double the amount of Vulnerable applied by Assassinate.
Spending Stars to play **Astral Pulse** triggers Black Hole, Child of the Stars, and Galactic Dust.
This will also trigger Mini Regent, provided it's the first instance of spending Stars for the turn.
Any 0 cost card that draws cards will accelerate Automation's gain, such as Prepared, Fetch, and FTL.
1 cost cards can also help towards Automation if they draw a lot of cards, such as Acrobatics and Skim.
Power cards with draw effects, such as Vicious and Pagestorm, can also facilitate it.
notes: The counter on the Automation buff counts down from 10 and indicates how many more cards must be drawn in order to gain .
Adding cards from the Draw Pile to the Hand without drawing them (such as by Secret Weapon) will not count down Automation.
Playing **Automation** multiple times creates multiple separate instances of Automation, each with a separate counter. All instances count down simultaneously when drawing cards.

For instance, if the player plays **Automation**, then draws 3 cards, then plays a second **Automation**, they will have 2 instances of Automation. The first's counter will be at 7, and the second's will be at 10.
If the Hand is too full to draw cards, any missed draws will not count down Automation.

synergies: **BEGONE!** is a simple and reliable way to trigger card-creation synergies like Pillar of Creation and Arsenal. Unlike CHARGE!! and GUARDS!!!, it also draws to replace itself.

Even without these synergies, **BEGONE!** is useful in most decks to remove basic Strikes and Defends to increase card quality. It can also Transform harmful {{{3}}} and Curse cards like Beckon and Debt to avoid their end-of-turn effects.
Creating a Minion Strike triggers Regalite, gaining 2 [Defend intent] Block.
Strike Dummy and Strike Dummy??? increase **Minion Strike's** damage by 3 and 1, respectively.
Vitruvian Minion doubles the final damage damage dealt by the Minion Strike.

Since **BEGONE!** is effectively two card plays in one (**BEGONE!** itself plus the Minion Strike), it can more easily trigger effects that track the types or number of cards played each turn, such as Rainbow Ring and Brilliant Scarf.
notes: **BEGONE!** leaves the Hand when played. It cannot Transform itself.
Transforming a card in Hand with **BEGONE!** is mandatory. As long as the player has another card in Hand besides **BEGONE!** itself, they must Transform it.
If there are no other cards in Hand to Transform, **BEGONE!** resolves with no effect.
Any type of card can be Transformed, including Status, Curse, and Quest cards.

synergies: Assassinate and/or Bag of Marbles ensure that Backstab will benefit from additional Vulnerable damage (provided the enemy does not have Artifact).
**Bad Luck'**s HP loss effect can be avoided in some ways: Cards such as Burning Pact, Prepared, or BEGONE! can discard, Exhaust, or Transform **Bad Luck** while it is in hand.
**Bad Luck'**s HP loss effect can be avoided in some ways: Cards like Havoc, CHARGE!!, and Cleanse can Exhaust or Transform **Bad Luck** while it is in the draw pile.
**Bad Luck'**s HP loss effect can be avoided in some ways: Apparition, Wraith Form, or Ghost in a Jar provide the Intangible buff which can reduce the HP loss from 13 to 1.
anti: Bing Bong will give the player a second **Bad Luck** when selecting **[Shatter]** in Reflections snoitcelfeR. At the same time, it will effectively triple the deck's size rather than double it, so it may not be a big downside.

synergies: Call of the Void creates a random card in Hand each turn and adds Ethereal to it.
Sentry Mode creates a Sweeping Gaze in Hand each turn, which is free to play and Ethereal.
Sculpting Strike adds Ethereal to any other card in Hand.
Veilpiercer makes the next Ethereal card free to play.
**Banshee's Cry** can reduce its cost after Transfigure adds Replay to it and increases its cost.

Alternatively, if the player has already played 5 Ethereal cards this combat (or 4 if **Banshee's Cry** is Upgraded), Transfigure will add Replay to it without changing its cost. This is likely a bug.
Big Hat creates two random cards with Ethereal in Hand at the start of each combat.
Music Box creates an Ethereal copy of the first Attack played each turn.
Ghost Seed adds Ethereal to all Strikes and Defends.
Spectral Knight's Hex makes ALL cards Ethereal, making **Banshee's Cry** reduce its cost much faster than normally possible.
notes: If the player is Confused by Snecko Eye or Snecko Eye??? or if **Banshee's Cry** has Slither, its cost randomizes each time it is drawn and overwrites any reduction it had, effectively causing it to "forget" about any Ethereal cards previously played this combat.
If the player plays an Ethereal Osty Attack while Osty is dead, that will still reduce **Banshee's Cry's** cost.
The only Osty Attack that is normally Ethereal is Sweeping Gaze (created by Sentry Mode), but Sculpting Strike and Call of the Void may add Ethereal to other cards.

If **Banshee's Cry** becomes free to play this turn (such as by Mummified Hand), it still properly tracks what its cost should be after it stops being free (including if any Ethereal cards were played while it was free).
If **Banshee's Cry** is created mid-combat, such as by an Attack Potion, its cost will be reduced by any Ethereal cards that were played before it was created.

synergies: Impervious and The Gambit gain huge amounts of [Defend intent] Block which will likely leave some excess for the next turn.
Unmovable doubles the first [Defend intent] Block gained from a card each turn.
Prolong and Entrench can double the accumulated [Defend intent] Block.
Accumulating excess [Defend intent] Block can make Body Slam extremely powerful.
Colossus and Uppercut reduce enemies' damage to stockpile [Defend intent] Block more easily. With both of them active, the enemy deals just 37.5% of its normal damage.
Barricade allows the player to get full value out of Plating from Stone Armor, Eternal Armor, and Heart of Iron.

Demon Form automatically gains Strength between turns and allows the player to focus solely on [Defend intent] Block early. Once enough [Defend intent] Block is gained, the player can attack freely for high damage.
anti: Because Barricade favors a more defensive playstyle, fights may take longer than usual. HP-loss cards and effects (especially automatic ones like Inferno and Crimson Mantle) may end up costing more HP than they're worth.

synergies: Vulnerable applied by this card: Increases damage dealt by Bully.
Vulnerable applied by this card: Grants an additional hit from Dismantle.
Vulnerable applied by this card: Grants additional Strength from Dominate.
Vulnerable applied by this card: Draws 1 (2) card via Vicious.

Intimidating Helmet grants 4 [Defend intent] Block whenever this card is played.
notes: If Bash has already been upgraded and/or Enchanted, Break will be upgraded and/or Enchanted by default.

synergies: Cards such as Secret Weapon and Secret Technique can still be played with No Draw in effect, as their search action is not considered drawing.
order: Battle Trance draws three cards, resolves any effects from drawing those cards, then applies No Draw. This means that if it draws Pommel Strike after Hellraiser has been played, then **Pommel Strike** will be played automatically before No Draw is applied and will draw an additional card.

notes: Beacon of Hope only appears when playing Multiplayer.
If a chosen Attack card has a single target, it will play against a random enemy.

**Beat Down** chooses its random Attack cards when played, but they are put into play one by one instead of all at once (unlike a card like Cascade or Knife Trap). As a result, the effects of selected Attack cards can alter the contents of the Discard Pile during **Beat Down's** resolution, although the Attacks chosen to play will not change.

If a selected Attack is moved to a different zone during **Beat Down's** resolution (such as Headbutt placing it on top of the Draw Pile), that selected Attack will play from its current zone instead.
If an Attack that costs X or is selected (such as Whirlwind or Stardust), the card will play for the current value of X, but no or are spent.
For example, if the player has 3 unspent , Whirlwind will play for X = 3.

synergies: Astral Pulse, Radiate, Stardust, and Seven Stars are all useful multi-hit Attacks for Star-focused decks, allowing **Beat into Shape** to fit in well.
Lunar Blast hits once for each Skill played this turn.
Make It So can return to the Hand multiple times per turn and costs 0 .
Minion Strikes and Minion Dive Bombs both cost 0 .
notes: **Beat into Shape** displays how much it will Forge when hovering over an enemy with it.
Each individual hit from Attacks contributes to **Beat into Shape's** Forge.
Hits that were [Defend intent] blocked or dealt no damage (such as due to Hardened Shell or negative Strength) still count.
Only damage from Attacks count as hits.
**Beat into Shape** does not count its own hit towards its Forge.
In Multiplayer, **Beat into Shape** does not count hits from Attacks played by other players.

synergies: Since Beckon is a Status card, it interacts with the following: Compact will Transform all Beckons in Hand into Fuel.
Since Beckon is a Status card, it interacts with the following: Iteration will draw 2 (3) cards when Beckon is drawn, if it is the first Status card drawn this turn.
Since Beckon is a Status card, it interacts with the following: Flak Cannon will Exhaust ALL Beckons in the Hand, Draw Pile, and Discard Pile and deals 8 (11) damage for each one.
**Beckon's** HP loss triggers Inferno and Rupture and increases Tear Asunder's hit count.
Cards like True Grit and Burning Pact can Exhaust Beckon.
BEGONE!, CHARGE!!, and GUARDS!!! can Transform Beckons into more useful cards.
notes: Beckon causes direct HP loss and ignores [Defend intent] Block.
Beckon discards itself when it causes HP loss, even if it is Retained by an effect like Convergence.
If Beckon gains Ethereal from Sculpting Strike, it causes HP loss before it Exhausts.
Believe in You only appears when playing Multiplayer.

synergies: **Biased Cognition** is a powerful card that requires the player to win the fight soon after playing it. Ideally, the player should have their Orbs of choice already Channeled to immediately benefit from the Focus.
Hologram can recover **Biased Cognition** from the Discard Pile if it is drawn before Orb setup is complete.
Cards that Channel a lot of Orbs in quick succession are very powerful with **Biased Cognition**, such as Tempest and Trash to Treasure.
Because **Big Bang+** is Innate, it works well with other Innate cards like Tyranny+ or Mad Science+.
With cards like Refine Blade and Hegemony, **Big Bang** can effectively save the gained for next turn.
Convergence can Retain **Big Bang** for next turn if it isn't needed this turn, or **Big Bang** can be spent this turn to gain to play Convergence and draw a card to be Retained.
**Big Bang** is a reasonable Replay target for Decisions, Decisions and Hidden Gem.
The first-turn drawbacks of Bread and Big Mushroom can be partially offset by **Big Bang+**.
**Big Bang's** free utility makes it suitable for Burning Sticks, which creates a copy of **Big Bang** in Hand if it is the first Skill Exhausted this combat.
If **Big Bang** is Enchanted with Clone from Pael's Growth, the player can copy it many times.
By Cloning **Big Bang+**, up to 10 **Big Bangs+** will be in the opening Hand each combat, guaranteeing 10 additional and , 10 cards in Hand, and a 60-damage Sovereign Blade.
Dolly's Mirror can add a copy of **Big Bang** into the deck upon pickup, and is especially useful if copying a **Bing Bang** that has Clone.
notes: **Big Bang** Forges after drawing a card. If the Hand is full due to the card draw and the Forge creates a Sovereign Blade, the Sovereign Blade will be sent to the Discard Pile.

synergies: The ideal use for Black Hole is in a deck that gains and spends as often as possible, especially with cards that also have low costs.
Alignment notably spends while gaining to play more cards at a time.
The Sealed Throne is incredibly powerful with Black Hole, dealing damage to all enemies for every card played.
notes: Black Hole only triggers once per instance of gaining or spending , regardless of how many were gained or spent.
If Black Hole triggers due to playing a card with a cost, it will deal damage after that card fully resolves.
If that card also gains (such as Royal Gamble), Black Hole will trigger twice.
gained from The Sealed Throne are gained in a separate instance from gained from playing a card, triggering Black Hole twice.

Copying a Skill counts towards reducing Pinpoint's cost this turn.
Copying Skills counts as card plays for triggering Strangle, Afterimage and Serpent Form.
Razor Tooth Upgrades played Skills before they are played again by **Burst**, causing the second plays to always use the Upgraded versions of Skills.
anti: Several Skills have no effect when copied: Bullet Time: Neither the No Draw nor free card play effects stack from the first play.
Several Skills have no effect when copied: Scrawl: The player will already be at the limit from the first play.
Several Skills have no effect when copied: Restlessness: The player will already have cards in Hand from the first play.
Several Skills have no effect when copied: Similarly, drawing an Attack with Impatience will cause the second play to have no effect.
Several Skills have no effect when copied: Anointed: All Rare cards from the Draw Pile will already be in Hand from the first play.
Several Skills have no effect when copied: Enlightenment: All cards in Hand will already have reduced costs from the first play.
Several Skills have no effect when copied: Apotheosis: All cards will already be Upgraded from the first play.

Similarly, several Skills have detrimental effects when copied: Hidden Daggers: The second play occurs immediately after the original play resolves and creates Shivs. If the player doesn't have enough other cards in Hand, they must discard one or both Shivs.
Similarly, several Skills have detrimental effects when copied: Storm of Steel: The second play discards all Shivs created by the first.
Similarly, several Skills have detrimental effects when copied: Panic Button: The second play gains no [Defend intent] Block but still applies 2 extra turns of No Block.

synergies: At least one source of gain is necessary to play **Bury**: Friendship and Demesne are the most accessible sources of continuous gain each turn.
At least one source of gain is necessary to play **Bury**: Invoke and Delay gain Energy Next Turn.
At least one source of gain is necessary to play **Bury**: Wisp, Borrowed Time, and Neurosurge gain when played.
At least one source of gain is necessary to play **Bury**: Many Ancient Relics gain each turn.
**Bury's** high base damage makes it scale well with damage multipliers like Lethality and Vulnerable.
**Bury** will always benefit from being Confused by Snecko Eye / Snecko Eye??? or from the Slither Enchantment.
Brilliant Scarf from Nonupeipe can make **Bury** free if 4 other cards are played before it this turn.
**Bury** deals so much damage that the Strength loss from Friendship and Shared Fate is negligible.

notes: Having **Byrdonis Egg** prevents Pael from offering Pael's Legion at the start of Act 2.
As long as there are at least 2 cards currently in the Draw Pile, the player must choose 2 of them to Transform and cannot choose fewer.
If there is only 1 card in the Draw Pile, it is the only card to be Transformed.
If the Draw Pile is empty, **CHARGE!!** resolves with no effect.
The player is allowed to select a Minion Dive Bomb in the Draw Pile to Transform, if one already exists.
This still triggers anything that triggers when a card is created.
The Draw Pile is not shuffled when Transforming cards this way. The chosen cards are Transformed without changing the order of cards.
Any type of card can be Transformed, including Status and Curse cards.

synergies: The Silent's Sly decks usually discard and redraw many cards each turn.
The Necrobinder's Souls are useful card draw, and Glimpse Beyond and Soulbound allow her to give Souls to other players.

Several 0 cost cards exist that draw to replace themselves, such as Escape Plan, Fetch, FTL, Flash of Steel, and Finesse. These all count towards Cacophony when they draw a card in addition to their usual minor effects.
notes: Cacophony counts all card draw for any reason, including all players' draws at the start of each turn.
If draws are skipped due to the Hand being too full, those skipped draws will not count towards Cacophony.
Playing **Cacophony** multiple times creates multiple separate instances of Cacophony, each of which tracks card draw individually.

The counter on the Cacophony buff shows how many cards must be drawn to trigger its damage, not how much damage will be dealt. This makes Cacophony gained from **Cacophony** and **Cacophony+** indistinguishable at a glance.
Cacophony triggers and resets its counter immediately after a player draws the 33rd card, including if the 33rd card is drawn in the middle of a large draw like Prophesize.

synergies: Multiple stacks of Stampede can play the card created by the first use of Stampede.
order: Created Attack can't be exhausted by Thrash.

synergies: The extra damage added by Calcify is not affected by Strength reduction from Friendship and Shared Fate or if the player is Weak.
Rattle is the only multi-hit Osty Attack and becomes much more powerful with Calcify.
Poke, Flatten, Fetch, and Right Hand Hand all can deal extra damage with Calcify for free.
**Calculated Gamble** is extremely valuable for Sly cards and can discard multiple at once for free. Even outside of Sly decks, it is very useful for redrawing a bad hand (especially when Upgraded).
Using other cards to draw a large hand before playing **Calculated Gamble** can trigger Speedster and Corrosive Wave many times in one turn.
In a pinch, cards that create multiple Shivs (such as Blade Dance and Leading Strike) can be used as extra draws for **Calculated Gamble** by purposefully discarding the Shivs.

Ring of the Snake and Bag of Preparation draw extra cards at the start of each combat, making it more likely to draw **Calculated Gamble** and giving it more cards to discard. This makes it much easier to find key Powers like Serpent Form and Tracking on the first turn, in addition to potentially triggering more Sly cards.
Tingsha deal 3 damage to a random enemy per card discarded.
Tough Bandages gain 3 [Defend intent] Block per card discarded.
Burning Sticks can create a copy of **Calculated Gamble** if it's the first Skill Exhausted this combat.
With **Calculated Gamble+** or Well-Laid Plans, the copy can be Retained for a later turn.
notes: **Calculated Gamble** leaves the Hand when played. It does not discard itself or count itself towards the number of cards drawn.

synergies: Playing cards generated by Call of the Void contribute to the amount of hits for Pull from Below.
An Ethereal version of Pull from Below will add to the hit count after being played.
Veilpiercer can discount the cost of cards generated by Call of the Void with the exception of X-Cost cards.
If Undeath is generated by Call of the Void all created copies will inherit the Ethereal property, which can be potent with other Ethereal synergies.
Playing cards generated by Call of the Void will discount the cost of Banshee's Cry.
Playing cards generated by Call of the Void will activate Spirit of Ash, granting [Defend intent] Block per Stack.
Cards generated by Call of the Void provide additional options for Oblivion, especially as it can generate 0 cost cards.
Playing cards generated by Call of the Void allows them to be redrawn, triggering Pagestorm and drawing 1 card per Stack.
The initial generation is not counted as a draw and does not activate Pagestorm.
Not playing cards generated by Call of the Void will progress the counter of Joss Paper at the end of your turn, potentially drawing additional cards for your next turn.
Not playing cards generated by Call of the Void will activate Forgotten Soul and deal 1 damage to a random enemy.
anti: Eradicate, Sow, Reap etc. can not utilize the Retain effect, when generated by Call of the Void.

synergies: **Caltrops** can contribute chip damage even when playing defensively, slightly speeding up fights.
Against enemies that hit multiple times or multiple enemies at once, **Caltrops** can contribute a much larger amount of damage.
Thorns gained from **Caltrops** stack with other sources of Thorns, such as Abrasive and Bronze Scales.
notes: **Caltrops** does not count as a Colorless card and cannot be copied with Heirloom Hammer.

synergies: Since **Capture Spirit** creates so many Souls at once, it is a strong enabler for synergies like Haunt and Soul Storm.

Even without Soul or Exhaust synergies, **Capture Spirit** effectively draws a total of 6 (8) cards. This greatly accelerates deck cycling, allowing the player to find important cards sooner. With a thin enough deck, **Capture Spirit** itself can be redrawn quickly to cycle the deck rapidly.
notes: **Capture Spirit** causes HP loss, not damage. As a result, it is not affected by damage-altering effects ( Strength, Weak, Vulnerable, etc.) and bypasses the enemy's [Defend intent] Block.
However, it does not bypass effects that limit HP loss, like Slippery and Hardened Shell.
The Souls are added to the Draw Pile without changing the order of other cards. Each Soul is simply inserted into the Draw Pile in a random place.

synergies: Both Bloodletting and Forgotten Ritual gain immediately.
Bloodletting can also be played multiple times per combat to fuel **Cascade** and other cards.
Headbutt can return a card from the Discard Pile to the top of the Draw Pile, guaranteeing that **Cascade** will play it.
If **Cascade** plays One-Two Punch, the next Attack card (or next 2 Attacks with One-Two Punch+) will be copied, including any Attacks played by **Cascade** itself.
**Cascade** plays cards directly from the Draw Pile without drawing them, so it ignores No Draw from Battle Trance.
However, if it plays any cards that draw cards, those draws will still be negated by No Draw.
Nostalgia returns the first Attack or Skill played each turn to the top of the Draw Pile, allowing **Cascade** to play that card again.
If **Cascade** itself is the first Attack or Skill played this turn, it returns to the top of the Draw Pile for next turn.
Intimidating Helmet gains 4 [Defend intent] Block if **Cascade** is played for 2 or more, as well as anytime **Cascade** plays a card that costs 2 or more.
Chemical X increases the value of X by 2. Even if **Cascade** is played for 0 , it will play the top 2 (3) cards of the Draw Pile.

**Cascade's** cost does not change even when Confused by the Snecko Eye or Snecko Eye???. This makes it valuable for decks using one of these Relics (especially since these decks already play powerful high-cost cards).
anti: Playing an Attack card with **Cascade** will use up Free Attack from Unrelenting.
Certain cards that require setup, proper timing, and/or a specific target may be forcibly played by **Cascade**: Body Slam deals little to no damage without existing [Defend intent] Block.
Certain cards that require setup, proper timing, and/or a specific target may be forcibly played by **Cascade**: Molten Fist and Dominate may target an enemy with few or no Vulnerable stacks.

Certain cards that require setup, proper timing, and/or a specific target may be forcibly played by **Cascade**: Whirlwind will deal no damage (since **Cascade** will have spent all available , causing Whirlwind to play for 0).

Certain cards that require setup, proper timing, and/or a specific target may be forcibly played by **Cascade**: Panic Button and The Gambit gain a large amount of [Defend intent] Block this turn but make later turns harder to survive.
Certain cards that require setup, proper timing, and/or a specific target may be forcibly played by **Cascade**: Feed and Hand of Greed go to waste if they do not kill an enemy.

Certain cards that require setup, proper timing, and/or a specific target may be forcibly played by **Cascade**: Anything that Exhausts cards in Hand will forcibly do so: True Grit and Cinder will Exhaust a random card in Hand.

Certain cards that require setup, proper timing, and/or a specific target may be forcibly played by **Cascade**: Anything that Exhausts cards in Hand will forcibly do so: Thrash will Exhaust a random Attack card in Hand.

Certain cards that require setup, proper timing, and/or a specific target may be forcibly played by **Cascade**: Anything that Exhausts cards in Hand will forcibly do so: True Grit+ and Brand force the player to choose a card in Hand to Exhaust.

Certain cards that require setup, proper timing, and/or a specific target may be forcibly played by **Cascade**: Anything that Exhausts cards in Hand will forcibly do so: Second Wind will Exhaust all non-Attack cards in Hand.

Certain cards that require setup, proper timing, and/or a specific target may be forcibly played by **Cascade**: Anything that Exhausts cards in Hand will forcibly do so: Fiend Fire and Stoke will Exhaust the entire Hand.
order: **Cascade** plays cards from the Draw Pile top to bottom (even though its animation appears to stack cards in the reverse order).
notes: When played, **Cascade** takes the top X cards of the Draw Pile, then puts them all into play at once without paying their costs.
Each of those cards that targets a single character or enemy will play against a random valid target.

All the cards are put into play at once when **Cascade** is played. If cards are drawn or returned to the Draw Pile during **Cascade's** resolution (such as if **Cascade** plays Battle Trance or Headbutt), the remaining cards to play do not change.
Each card played by **Cascade** is discarded immediately after being played. **Cascade** itself will resolve and discard once all those other cards are played and resolved.

If X is greater than the number of cards remaining in the Draw Pile, **Cascade** will put all cards in the Draw Pile into play, then reshuffle the Discard Pile and put the remainder from the newly-shuffled Draw Pile.
However, if X is greater than the total number of cards in both the Draw and Discard Piles, **Cascade** will put all those cards into play, but any excess value of X goes to waste.
If **Cascade** attempts to play an Unplayable card, that card is sent to Discard Pile with no effect. It does not count as a card play.
If **Cascade** itself is played by a card's effect (such as Havoc or another **Cascade** card), the value of X is equal to the player's current , but no will be spent.

synergies: **Catastrophe** (particularly if Upgraded) can be a strong target for Pael's Growth, as each copy can target other copies, which then target other copies. With a high enough density of cloned **Catastrophes**, playing a single copy will often automatically play every card in the draw pile.
Having a high number of expensive cards in the deck increases the chances that **Catastrophe** will play something worth its Energy cost.
Snecko Eye also works well with expensive cards, and **Catastrophe** itself is more likely to have its cost lowered than raised when randomized by Confused.
Playing **Catastrophe** triggers Danse Macabre and Intimidating Helmet to gain [Defend intent] Block. Any cards played by **Catastrophe** that cost 2+ will also trigger them.
notes: Cards that target a single character or enemy will play against random valid targets.

**Catastrophe** fully resolves each card before choosing a new one to play. If the played card's effect changes the contents of the Draw Pile (such as by drawing cards or returning cards to the Draw Pile), that may affect which card is next played by **Catastrophe**.

Unplayable cards will not be chosen to play, unless all cards in the Draw Pile are Unplayable. In this case, **Catastrophe** attempts to play random Unplayable cards in the Draw Pile, discarding them with no effect.
Unplayable cards "played" this way do not count as card plays.
If **Catastrophe** would play more cards than are currently in the Draw Pile, it plays as many as possible, but it does not reshuffle the Draw Pile.

If **Catastrophe** plays a card that costs X or (such as Whirlwind or Stardust), the card will play for the current value of X (e.g. if the player has 3 unspent ), Whirlwind will play for X = 3), but no or are spent.

synergies: **Celestial Might's** hit count makes it scale well with anything that gains Strength or Vigor, such as Patter and Arsenal.

notes: Energy Next Turn gained from **Charge Battery** stacks with other sources, such as Scavenge and other copies of **Charge Battery**.

synergies: Exhausting Drum of Battle immediately gains (3 ).
Exhausting Howl from Beyond causes it to play automatically from the Exhaust Pile at the end of this turn.
Intimidating Helmet gains 4 [Defend intent] Block whenever **Cinder** is played.
anti: Playing **Cinder** runs the risk of Exhausting an unintended card. Playing valuable cards before **Cinder** guarantees they will not be Exhausted, but **Cinder's** cost leaves less for playing those cards and/or playing around the Exhausted card.
Cards and effects like Havoc and Stampede that automatically play cards may forcibly play **Cinder** and Exhaust a valuable card.
notes: **Cinder** leaves the Hand when played. It will never Exhaust itself.
**Cinder** can still be played when no other cards are in Hand, in which case no card is Exhausted.

synergies: Second Wind can Exhaust all non-Attack cards in Hand.
Corruption and Ghost Seed can fill a similar role to a lesser degree, Exhausting many Skill cards or Defends, respectively.
Targeted Exhaust effects like True Grit+ and Purity can remove cards in the same Hand as **Clash**.
anti: Unlike most cards and strategies, **Clash** pairs very poorly with card draw, since drawing non-Attack cards makes it unplayable.
Card draw from Relics and Powers is also generally mandatory, such as Vicious, Dark Embrace, Pendulum, and Joss Paper. These effects may force non-Attack cards into the Hand.
As **Clash** is not visually colorless, it cannot be duplicated via Heirloom Hammer, despite being a colorless card.
notes: Any card that isn't an Attack will prevent **Clash** from being playable, including Status, Curse, and Quest cards.
If **Clash** is forcibly played by a card or effect (such as Havoc, Stampede, or Distilled Chaos), it will play and deal damage even if there are non-Attack cards in Hand.

synergies: As Claw cards increase the damage of all Claw cards, multiple copies of Claw synergize with themselves.
Cards such as Hologram and All for One can be used to play Claw additional times before shuffling your deck again.
Reboot can also lead to Claw being drawn repeatedly.
Cards such as Secret Weapon, Stratagem, and Nostalgia (& the Perfect Fit Enchantment) can allow Claw to be drawn more consistently.
Effects that cause cards to be played multiple times, such as Echo Form or Replay will cause Claw to scale successively.

If other characters' cards are in the player's deck (via Prismatic Gem, Sea Glass, or certain events): Cards such as Headbutt and Cosmic Indifference allow Claw to be played more frequently. However, this will increase the amount of draws needed before the deck is shuffled, making them generally inferior to cards such as Hologram.
History Course can replay Claw, provided it was the last Attack played on the prior turn.
Music Box creates an Ethereal copy of the first Attack played each turn.
Power Cell puts 2 random 0 cost cards into the player's hand at the start of each combat.
**Cleanse** is a very useful card due to its ability to remove unwanted cards from the Draw Pile, most notably basic Strikes and Defends.

**Cleanse** can also Exhaust Status, Curse, and Quest cards, making it somewhat safer to obtain these cards from Relics/Ancient Bonuses, Events or enemies mid-combat: Cursed Pearl, Hefty Tablet, Biiig Hug, Blessed Antler, Blood-Soaked Rose, Distinguished Cape and Calling Bell all add Curses or Statuses to the deck.

**Cleanse** can also Exhaust Status, Curse, and Quest cards, making it somewhat safer to obtain these cards from Relics/Ancient Bonuses, Events or enemies mid-combat: On Ascension 5 (Ascension 5+) and higher, the player always starts with Ascender's Bane in the deck.
If the player has Eidolon, **Cleanse** can Exhaust an Ethereal card from the Draw Pile for Eidolon to play.
In a pinch, **Cleanse** can Exhaust a Soul from the Draw Pile to increase Soul Storm's damage.
If **Cleanse** Exhausts a Skill, and no other Skills have been Exhausted this combat, Burning Sticks will create a copy of that card in Hand.
notes: As long as the Draw Pile contains any cards, Exhausting a card with **Cleanse** is mandatory.
If the Draw Pile is empty, **Cleanse** will still Summon, but no card will be Exhausted.

synergies: The damage of each Shiv will be increased by the amount of Accuracy you have, which can be obtained from Accuracy.
Anything that benefits from Exhaust will be triggered by playing Shivs.
Creating a Debris will increase damage dealt by Supermassive.
Creating a Debris triggers Arsenal, granting 1 Strength.
Creating a Debris triggers Pillar of Creation, granting 3 (4 if upgraded) [Defend intent] Block.
Creating a Debris triggers Regalite, granting 2 [Defend intent] Block.
Exhausting the Debris triggers Joss Paper and Forgotten Soul.
All cards that apply Vulnerable enable Colossus's damage reduction, making it much easier to block attacks while still dealing damage.

Taunt is the only [Defend intent] Block-gain card that applies Vulnerable. Together, it and **Colossus** effectively gain 20 [Defend intent] Block (or up to 28 effective [Defend intent] Block if both are Upgraded).
Thunderclap and Shockwave apply Vulnerable to ALL enemies, guaranteeing that Colossus will reduce damage from all of them this turn.
Shockwave also applies Weak for even more damage reduction.
Crimson Mantle and Sai gain [Defend intent] Block automatically each turn.
anti: **Colossus** is much less useful against enemies with Artifact, which prevents them from having Vulnerable applied. Over-reliance on **Colossus** can be a liability in these fights.
**Colossus** increases the player's survivability without actually gaining much [Defend intent] Block, putting it at odds with Body Slam (and Barricade, to an extent).
notes: Colossus multiplies with Weak, reducing the damage from enemies that are both Weak and Vulnerable by 62.5%.
In Multiplayer, it also multiplies with the damage modifiers from Tank or Guarded.
Having Colossus visually changes the damage numbers in the Intents of Vulnerable enemies to show the actual amount of damage taken.
If **Colossus** is played multiple times in one turn, the Colossus buff will carry over for multiple consecutive turns.

synergies: **Compact** can help recover the lost to Void from TURBO.
Gunk Up and Fight Through create Slimed and Wounds, respectively. These are not Ethereal and will stay in the deck even if drawn without **Compact**.
Iteration is very powerful with **Compact**, making it possible to draw many Statuses at once.

Even outside a Status-focused deck, **Compact** is useful for dealing with enemies that create Status cards (such as Vantom and Soul Fysh), and Compact+ can gain a respectable amount of [Defend intent] Block for its cost in other fights.
notes: Only Status cards are Transformed into Fuel. Curse and Quest cards are unaffected.

synergies: Since Zap is always a part of the starting deck, anything that can Channel a non- Lightning Orb can enable **Compile Driver** to draw 2 cards.
Rainbow Channels Lightning, Frost, and Dark Orbs in one go.
Capacitor, Modded, and Runic Capacitor can gain additional Orb Slots for more unique Orbs.
anti: Cards and strategies that focus only on a single Orb type ( Tempest, Voltaic, Darkness, etc.) will only draw a single card at best from **Compile Driver**.
Bulk Up removes an Orb Slot, leaving less room for unique Orbs.
Shatter Evokes ALL Orbs when played, requiring time and resources to build up more unique Orbs again.
notes: The unique Orb types are Lightning, Frost, Dark, Plasma, and Glass. With all 5 of these Orbs, **Compile Driver** will draw 5 cards.
Note that this requires gaining at least 2 additional Orb Slots.
If no Orbs are currently Channeled, **Compile Driver** draws no cards.

synergies: Any Attack that hits multiple times can singlehandedly apply large amounts of Poison, such as Conflagration, Radiate, and Pull from Below.
**Concoct** can freely enable Mirage if another player can hit the enemy enough times in one turn.
If the targeted ally has applied enough Poison, Outbreak is a powerful follow-up to trigger its damage immediately (in addition to any damage that was dealt by that ally's Attacks).
notes: Each instance of unblocked Attack damage triggers Concoct to apply Poison.

The Concoct buff on the receiving player is the source of Poison, not **Concoct's** user. Effects like Snecko Skull and Sleight of Flesh will only trigger for the player who gained Concoct and not for **Concoct's** user.
Additionally, the Concoct buff (not the played Attack) is the source of Poison. It applies a separate instance of Poison from the played Attack and will not interact with Unsettling Lamp.
Osty Attacks are not affected by Concoct and will not apply Poison.

Concoct triggers immediately when the played Attack deals unblocked damage. Since most Attacks that apply debuffs deal their damage first (e.g. Bash), Concoct will apply its Poison first, which can remove Artifact from enemies before the Attack applies its own debuff(s).

synergies: Any card that Forges or otherwise powers up Sovereign Blade makes **Conqueror** increasingly effective.
Summon Forth can retrieve Sovereign Blade if it was used on a previous turn (although playing all three cards costs 4 total).

Any sources of Retain, such as Convergence or Equilibrium, make it possible to keep **Conqueror** in Hand until other damage boosts like Falling Star are drawn (or until Sovereign Blade itself is drawn, if it was previously played).
Having Parry makes it significantly safer to play both **Conqueror** and Sovereign Blade, especially if the player cannot gain extra .
In Multiplayer, all players' Sovereign Blades deal double damage to the enemy with Conqueror, making Hammer Time particularly powerful.
order: Conqueror multiplies with Vulnerable, making the enemy take triple damage from Sovereign Blade.
notes: Playing **Conqueror** against the same enemy multiple times in one turn causes that enemy to take double damage from Sovereign Blade for that many turns. It does not increase the damage it takes from Sovereign Blade further.

synergies: All of **Constellation's** effects are extremely powerful for supporting other players. The gain and card draw make it easier for the receiving player to play more or expensive cards, and the [Defend intent] Block gain makes it much safer to play Attack and Power cards instead of defending.
notes: The Dexterity and Frail on **Constellation's** user affect its [Defend intent] Block gain, and any Dexterity or Frail on the receiving ally have no effect.
If **Constellation's** user has Vambrace or Pael's Legion active, those will be used up and double the [Defend intent] Block gained by the receiving player.
Even if the receiving player has these effects active, they will not be used up or double **Constellation's** [Defend intent] Block gain.
If the receiving player has Shadowmeld, that will double the [Defend intent] Block gained from **Constellation**.

Even if **Constellation's** user has Shadowmeld, that will not double the [Defend intent] Block gained by the receiving player. Note that this is only possible if the Regent or Silent gains access to the other's cards, such as with Prismatic Gem.

synergies: **Consuming Shadow** requires some planning to maximize its value: the Dark Orbs will be prematurely Evoked if the player Channels too many new Orbs, but they will be automatically Evoked if the player fails to Channel any new Orbs.
Sources of Glass Orbs (especially Spinner) pair well with **Consuming Shadow**, since Glass Orbs should be Evoked as soon as possible to maximize their damage.
Lightning Rod will Channel a Lightning Orb for the next 2 turns.
anti: Plasma Orbs will be Evoked at the end of the turn after the player can play cards, wasting their .
Bulk Up reduces the player's Orb slots, giving the Dark Orbs less room to build up damage before they are automatically Evoked.
Cards that can Channel many Orbs at once (such as Chill, Tempest, Meteor Strike, and Voltaic) will forcibly Evoke the Dark Orbs.

Copying **Consuming Shadow** with effects like Echo Form or Signal Boost is detrimental: it will Channel so many Dark Orbs that some will immediately be Evoked, and twice as many Orbs will be Evoked at the end of the turn.
order: Consuming Shadow Evokes the leftmost Orb after all Orbs' effects have triggered.

synergies: **Convergence** can lead to explosive turns when combined with other setup cards like Glow, Hidden Cache, Hegemony, and Foregone Conclusion.

**Convergence** is especially powerful with Stardust and Heavenly Drill, since it allows them to hit an extra time (and makes it easier to double Heavenly Drill's power) and Retains them if they're already in Hand.
anti: **Convergence** will Retain all Debris created by Crash Landing if played in the same turn. If the player cannot make some space in Hand, they will not draw any cards next turn.
A similar situation can happen with Scrawl.
order: When playing **Convergence** multiple times in one turn, cards in Hand will be Retained for that many turns, but all the extra and will be gained on the next turn only.

synergies: Additional Orb Slots are needed to have all 5 unique Orbs Channeled at once, thereby gaining the maximum 10 (15) [Defend intent] Block from Coolant each turn.
Capacitor gains 2 (3) additional Orb Slots when played.
Modded gains 1 Orb Slot, draws 1 (2) card(s), and increases its cost by 1 when played.
Chaos and Trash to Treasure can diversify the player's Orbs. This is particularly valuable since Dark, Plasma, and Glass Orbs have fewer sources than Lightning and Frost Orbs.
Rainbow Channels a Lightning, Frost and Dark Orb, immediately giving the player 3 unique Orb types.
Runic Capacitor gains 3 additional Orb Slots at the start of each combat.
Symbiotic Virus will Channel 1 Dark Orb at the start of each combat, giving the player 2 unique Orb types to begin with instead of 1.
Potion of Capacity gains 2 additional Orb Slots when consumed.
anti: Losing an Orb Slot from Bulk Up limits the amount of unique Orbs that can be Channeled at once.
Shatter will Evoke all currently Channeled Orbs twice, leaving little time to prepare new Orbs for Coolant next turn.
order: Coolant gains [Defend intent] Block after automatic Channeling effects like Lightning Rod and Spinner. Those Channeled Orbs can count towards Coolant's [Defend intent] Block gain or Evoke other unique Orbs if there are not enough free Orb Slots.

synergies: Other players with 0 Attacks or multi-hit Attacks will benefit the most from **Coordinate**.
Damage multipliers like Vulnerable, Flanking, and Knockdown greatly increase **Coordinate's** effectiveness.

If the receiving player has Ruined Helmet and has not gained Strength this combat, the extra Strength gained from Ruined Helmet will not be removed. That player will gain 10 (16) Strength this turn and keeps 5 (8) of it for the rest of combat.
notes: Despite its wording of "give another player Strength," **Coordinate** does not reduce its user's Strength this turn.

synergies: Prepared+, Acrobatics, and Adrenaline are efficient sources of card draw for their cost.
Adrenaline and Brightest Flame gain in addition to drawing cards.
Scrawl can trigger Corrosive Wave many times at once when played with a near-empty Hand.
Calculated Gamble can discard a large Hand and draw the same amount of cards afterwards. In addition, Calculated Gamble+ has Retain to save it for when **Corrosive Wave** is in the Hand.
Reflex is unique in that it draws 2 (3) cards and has Sly, leading to free Corrosive Wave triggers when discarded.
With the use of Master Planner (and Hand Trick to smaller extent), almost any Skill which draws cards can gain Sly to trigger Corrosive Wave even more times during this turn.

synergies: Stratagem requires good draw power and/or a thin deck to make the most of it. Draw effects make the deck cycle faster, and Exhausting cards reduces the amount of cards that need to be cycled and can remove unwanted cards.

Photon Cut, Glimmer, and Thinking Ahead all draw cards and return a card to the top of the Draw Pile from the Hand. Stratagem triggers before returning a card, so the player can search a card and set it up to draw next turn.
Reboot allows the player to select ANY card from their deck (except an Exhausted card), then draw 4 (6) cards on top of that.

notes: Adding a card to the Hand with Stratagem does not count as a draw. Cards that care about card draw, such as Murder and Kingly Punch, will not be affected by it. If the player is Confused by Snecko Eye or Snecko Eye??? or the added card has Slither, its cost will not be randomized.

Creating or Transforming cards in the Draw Pile does not cause it to shuffle. Cards that are added are inserted randomly, and Transformed cards simply replace the originals. In both cases, the order of cards does not change, and Stratagem does not trigger.
The card added by Stratagem is in addition to whatever draw caused the Draw Pile to shuffle. It does not happen in place of any card draw.

Cards which deal more damage for each card with a certain attribute such as Perfected Strike, Crescent Spear, and Squeeze are exceptionally powerful if duplicated numerous times. Each copy will make all other copies stronger, meaning that each copy can potentially become powerful enough to kill bosses in a single hit.

Note that Crescent Spear can only be played three times without some source of additional Stars. Even if each copy played deals hundreds of damage, certain battles (specifically those against Exoskeletons and four Scrolls of Biting) require more than three hits to kill all enemies. One or more upgraded copies of Big Bang can guarantee that additional Stars are available at the beginning of each battle, and the Lunar Pastry can provide one additional Star each turn.
Cards that play other cards from the draw pile for free ( Catastrophe or Cascade) can allow you to play every card in the draw pile if duplicated enough times.

Uproar only plays one more card each time it's played, but with enough copies, and with most or all other attacks removed from the deck, playing a single **Uproar** can often automatically play another copy and start a chain reaction.

Cards like Flash of Steel or Adrenaline, which cost no and draw a card to replace themselves, are generally safe to clone, as there is usually no downside to having more of them in your deck. There are some exceptions, such as the battles against Hunter Killer or Entomancer, which can harm the player for each card played.
With the Game Piece, free-to-play powers like Panache can be effective cloning targets, as each copy played will draw an additional card.

With both **Game Piece** and Mummified Hand, any power can be a good target for **Pael's Growth**: each copy played will draw a card and make another copy free to play. The free copy will then draw another card and make another copy free to play.

Decks filled with cloned powers may struggle against the Globe Head, which damages the player for each power played. If you have too many cloned powers, even a deck capable of effortlessly winning the rest of the game may inevitably die if you happen to run into this enemy.

Globe Head can only possibly appear starting on the third normal combat of Act 3, so taking as few normal combats as possible (and, unless you have Juzu Bracelet, avoiding Unknown Location spaces as well) can make it much less likely that you will run into him.

**Snecko Eye** also removes the need to Upgrade cards whose costs change, such as Stampede or Tracking. However, if those cards are already upgraded, or if they become upgraded by something like Apotheosis or the Reflections snoitcelfeR event, then this upgrade is essentially wasted.

Bullet Time makes ALL cards in Hand free this turn, guaranteeing that the other 6 cards in Hand can be played regardless of how unlucky their costs are. Because the cost of **Bullet Time** will usually be reduced by **Snecko Eye**, it is often possible to draw additional cards using a card like Acrobatics and still play **Bullet Time** afterwards.
Graveblast, Dredge, and Hologram return cards directly from the Discard Pile to the Hand without randomizing their costs, allowing the player to reuse cheap cards.

anti: Retain effects ( Well-Laid Plans, Convergence, Snap, etc.) are much less useful with **Snecko Eye**. notes: All four outcomes of cost randomization have equal likelihood (a 25% chance for each cost), and the card's cost has no effect on the outcome.
This means that on average, all cards will cost 1.5 .
Confused only randomizes a card's cost when it is drawn from the Draw Pile. If it is added to the Hand by any means other than drawing it, its cost does not randomize.
Adding cards directly to the Hand from the Draw Pile (such as with Secret Weapon) does not count as drawing them and will not randomize their costs.

Randomizing a card's cost also overwrites any changes to its cost. The card's cost can be modified again after randomization, but that change will be lost once the card is drawn another time.

If a card becomes free to play this turn (such as with Bullet Time or Brilliant Scarf), its cost will return to the original amount after it's played or at the end of the turn, instead of returning to whatever its randomized cost was before it became free.

Lingering free-to-play effects ( Free Power, Free Skill, Void Form, and Veilpiercer) function differently from free-this-turn effects. Instead of changing cards' costs to 0 until the effect wears off, they allow the player to play a card without paying its cost (which is visually represented by appearing to change its cost to 0 ). The card's cost beneath the visual effect is still randomized, but it can be played regardless of that cost.

Dodge and Roll and Glitterstream both gain [Defend intent] Block immediately and Block Next Turn, both of which are doubled by **Vambrace**. Similarly, Toric Toughness gains [Defend intent] Block immediately and Toric Toughness for the next 2 turns, which are both doubled.

Cards that create or Transform cheap cards, such as Leading Strike and BEGONE!, will count multiple times towards **Velvet Choker's** limit.
notes: **Velvet Choker** counts cards that are not played directly from the Hand, such as when playing a card again in a row with an effect like One-Two Punch or Replay, or when playing a card using another card's effect like Havoc.
If the sixth card played this turn is played again in a row, the additional play(s) will still resolve, even though they exceed **Velvet Choker's** limit.

If a card's effect plays a card from another zone, such as Eidolon or Catastrophe, any cards that exceed **Velvet Choker's** limit will still be put into the Discard Pile after attempting to be played.
