useful: **Lagavulin Matriarch** gives the player three free turns to set up, making it easy to play expensive powers like Demon Form or Reaper Form.

[Debuff intent] [Buff intent] Soul Siphon permanently reduces the player's Strength and Dexterity by 2 each time it is used. Cards like Conflagration or Death's Door will be much weaker because this debuff affects each individual instance of damage or Block, while cards like Bury or Impervious will barely be affected.

The **Turret Operator'**s damage is split into multiple hits with low damage on each, so Strength reduction from cards like Piercing Wail, Shared Fate or Mangle will decrease his damage significantly and will often set it to 0.
The **Turret Operator** will take five times as much damage as most enemies from Thorns.
Cards like Fiend Fire, Compact and GUARDS!!! can get rid of all copies of Toxic in hand without needing to pay their Energy cost, and also gain an additional benefit from doing so.
Cards like Calculated Gamble or Storm of Steel can also get rid of Toxic and gain a benefit for doing so, although this means that Toxic will be drawn again once the deck is reshuffled.

notes: Hatch timer starts at 2 if summoned during the enemy turn, or 1 during the player turn.
Hatching removes all negative status effects which were applied to the **Tough Egg**.

useful: Any attack which hits all enemies, such as Sow or Dagger Spray, can deal a significant amount of damage.
Damaging the **Phantasmal Gardeners** indirectly through non-Attack cards will not trigger Skittish, so cards like Negative Pulse, Flame Barrier, Noxious Fumes, or Haze can be useful against them.

Sunder deals almost enough damage to kill a **Phantasmal Gardener** in one hit, so it can easily finish one off and refund its cost if a basic attack like Strike (Defect) was played on a previous turn.
If upgraded, **Sunder+** deals enough damage to instantly kill a **Phantasmal Gardener**.
notes: **Phantasmal Gardeners** gain Block after the first attack played against them resolves. For example, playing Twin Strike will deal 5 damage twice, then the **Phantasmal Gardener** will gain Block.

However, cards with **Replay** count as being played multiple times, so if an attack with **Replay** is played against a **Phantasmal Gardener** then it will gain Block after the first play and before the second one.

useful: Frontloaded damage cards like Perfected Strike, Backstab, and Defile can be useful for taking down the Phrog Parasite before it can create too many Infections. They can also finish off individual Wrigglers quickly.
Deathbringer, Deadly Poison, and other cards which apply Poison or Doom can gain an extra turn before the Wrigglers attack, if the Phrog Parasite dies to their damage.
Attacks which target all enemies like Dagger Spray, Bone Shards, and Whirlwind can damage all of the Wrigglers at once.
Inferno deals consistent damage to all enemies every turn. It also triggers whenever **Infections** deal unblocked damage.
Cards which can discard, Exhaust, or Transform **Infections**, such as Burning Pact or Hidden Daggers, can prevent them from dealing damage.
Compact and Flak Cannon are especially noteworthy, since they remove all **Infections** in Hand or in all zones, respectively.
notes: Whether the Wrigglers are [Stun intent] Stunned on the player's next turn depends on if the Phrog Parasite dies during the player turn or the enemy turn: If the Phrog Parasite is killed with an Attack card or damage from an Orb, the Wrigglers will be [Stun intent] Stunned during this turn, not the player's next turn.

Whether the Wrigglers are [Stun intent] Stunned on the player's next turn depends on if the Phrog Parasite dies during the player turn or the enemy turn: If the Phrog Parasite dies to Poison or Doom, then the Wrigglers will have no Intent when spawned. They will be [Stun intent] Stunned during the player's next turn.

Whether the Wrigglers are [Stun intent] Stunned on the player's next turn depends on if the Phrog Parasite dies during the player turn or the enemy turn: This also applies if the Phrog Parasite dies as a result of its own attack, such as by Thorns or Necro Mastery.
**Infections** deal damage during the player turn, so the damage will activate cards like Inferno or Rupture.

Omnislice damages the target, then damages all other enemies afterwards. If the first hit kills the **Phrog Parasite**, then it will spawn **Wrigglers** before the card resolves and the Wrigglers will also take damage.
After a Bound card is played, other Bound cards cannot be played that turn even with effects like Sly or a Duplicator.
Similarly, playing a Sly card that has Bound will prevent other Bound cards from being played.
Bound cards duplicated by effects like Music Box or Dual Wield will also be bound.
Transforming a Bound card during battle will remove Bound from it, allowing it to be played freely.
Bound cards are still unbound at the end of your turn even when Retained, allowing you to use cards such as Well-Laid Plans to play other bound cards on a later turn.
If a Bound card is played once, then returned to your hand in some way (ex. being redrawn), it still won't able to be played until end of turn.
If the Torch Head Amalgam dies after its turn to an effect like Doom, the Queen will immediately switch intents to [Attack3 intent] Off with Your Head, skipping the usual [Buff intent] Enrage .
If the Torch Head Amalgam is killed on Turn 2 or earlier, the Queen will not use [Buff intent] Enrage on her first cycle.
If the Scroll of Biting deals unblocked damage to Osty, neither he nor the player loses any max HP from Paper Cuts.
If Tungsten Rod reduces the unblocked damage taken from 1 to 0 (for example, if a **Scroll of Biting** deals 14 damage to a player with 13 [Defend intent] Block) then the player will not lose max HP.
If the Scroll of Biting dies from reflected damage such as Thorns or Flame Barrier while dealing unblocked damage to the player, the player will not lose any max HP from Paper Cuts.
Osty is not affected by Shrink and deals full damage with his own Attack cards.

Hardened Shell resets on both the start of the player's turn as well as the start of the Skulking Colony's turn. Since Poison deals damage at the start of an enemy's turn, it is possible to deal a maximum of 40 damage in a single turn by doing 20 attack damage and having 20 stacks of Poison on it at the same time.
Thorns, Reflect, Flame Barrier, Necro Mastery, and Demise also trigger on the enemy turn.
Hardened Shell can be partially bypassed by The Boot. If the enemy can only lose 1 to 4 more HP this turn, hitting it with an Attack will cause it to take 5 damage instead of the limited amount.
Any further Attacks this turn will still deal 0 damage and will not be affected.

useful: Anything which can get rid of Beckon without playing it can be useful. Transforming or exhausting it through cards like Fiend Fire or BEGONE! is best because it will be permanently removed rather than simply being put into the discard pile, but discarding it with cards like Prepared or Hidden Daggers can still save Energy compared to playing it normally.
Cards like No Escape which apply Doom rather than dealing damage can ignore Intangible.
notes: The first iteration of [Buff intent] Fade's Intangible fades instantly during the transition from Soul Fysh's turn to the player's. It effectively gains just 1 Intangible.
Since Nightmare creates cards at the start of your turn, upgraded cards duplicated by Nightmare are not affected by Dampen.
Each of Test Subject's phases will lose all status effects when transitioning to the next phase, including the Strength gained from Enrage in the first phase.
Cards with on-kill or Fatal triggers ( Feed, The Hunt, Knockout Blow, Sunder, and Hand of Greed) will trigger successfully during any of the Test Subject's phases.

Because the Test Subject is a Boss in Act 3, after which there are no opportunities to spend Gold or earn card rewards, Feed, Knockout Blow, and Sunder are the only cards with an on-kill or Fatal trigger that matters.
After Test Subject loses all its HP in a phase, it cannot be targeted by any cards until it revives into the next phase.

Cards with no targets can still be played, including Attack cards that hit all enemies or random enemies (such as Sword Boomerang or Sweeping Beam), but they will deal no damage. All other possible effects will still occur (for instance, Sweeping Beam will still draw a card).

useful: Iteration will trigger consistently during this battle because the player's deck starts with six copies of Frantic Escape shuffled in.
Flak Cannon will hit an additional six times the first time it is played, but using it can be very risky because you will be left with no way to gain more Sandpit through Frantic Escapes.
notes: Sandpit acts like a Debuff on each player, it was likely placed on **The Insatiable** to improve visibility of the debuff
Fairy in a Bottle and Lizard Tail will not prevent the death stemming from Sandpit
If the enemy escapes, the player does not receive any gold, but still gets a card reward and a possible potion drop.
The card stolen by Swipe follows a set order of priority: 1. Non- Imbued Uncommon cards
The card stolen by Swipe follows a set order of priority: 2. Non- Imbued Rare, Common, and Event cards
The card stolen by Swipe follows a set order of priority: 3. Non- Imbued Basic and Quest cards
The card stolen by Swipe follows a set order of priority: 4. Ancient cards or cards that are Imbued
The card stolen by Swipe follows a set order of priority: 5. Curse cards

Only cards currently in the player's draw or discard pile when the move is used will be selected. This means under the right circumstances the move can be utilized to remove Eternal cards from the player's deck.
The returned card can be skipped, which means it is possible to defeat the Thieving Hopper, receive all the usual combat rewards and still have a card removed if it is so desired.
When choosing to take back the stolen card, all the usual interactions on adding a card to the deck apply (e.g. Bing Bong, or Lucky Fysh).

Token cards and Status cards can never be stolen as this would result in being able to add a temporary card into your deck permanently. This also applies to other temporary cards, such as those created by potions.
Despite its name, the Two-Tailed Rat doesn't visually have two tails and instead has one tail that is forked at the end.
The Fungi Beasts from Slay the Spire 1 appear to be Two-Tailed Rats corpses with a fungal infection controlling them.

useful: Multi-hit attacks like Conflagration or Lunar Blast are effective at removing Slippery stacks quickly.

Even small amounts of Poison can consistently remove a stack of Slippery each turn. With Accelerant, it will remove 2 (3 if Upgraded) stacks per turn, as long as Vantom has enough stacks of Poison for all instances to activate.
Consistent damage over time from cards like Inferno or relics like Mercury Hourglass can help remove Slippery faster.
Cards like Stoke or BEGONE! can remove Wound from your deck.
Damaging non-attack cards like Deadly Poison or Inferno are not affected by **Tangled** and can be played for their normal price.

Even if you can defeat the **Waterfall Giant**, its final [DeathBlow intent] Explode move can still easily kill you. Strong block cards like Blood Wall or Leg Sweep can be played on the final turn to block some of the damage from the explosion.

Increasing the block density of your deck over the course of the battle makes it less likely that you will draw a hand full of non-block cards when the **Waterfall Giant** uses [DeathBlow intent] Explode. Cards like Burning Pact and BEGONE! can be used to remove non-block cards like Strike.
Anger can be dangerous to play during this battle, as it increases the number of attack cards in your deck and makes it more likely that you will end up with few or no block cards on the final turn.
Necrobinder's Summon cards, such as Bodyguard and Afterlife, can use Osty to block damage on the final turn no matter which cards you happen to draw.
Cards like Well-Laid Plans and Convergence can hold block cards in hand to save them for the final turn.
notes: Even though the HP bar in the last phase shows as "infinity", it is actually set to the finite number of 999,999,999 HP. As such, it is theoretically possible to kill the Waterfall Giant in its last phase.
If a card both deals damage and applies a debuff like Neutralize, the damage can kill the **Waterfall Giant** and activate [Stun intent] About To Blow, then the debuff will be applied.
